analysis: Integration review of the model-download cancellation fix. Production change: provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Models/StreamingFileDownloadDelegate.swift (attach at head lines ~82-89, finish at ~91-100). The `resumed` flag is replaced by a stored first-terminal `result`. `attach` resumes immediately if completion already arrived; `finish` records only the first result under the lock and resumes outside the lock. Either ordering resumes the continuation exactly once, duplicates are ignored, and there is no lock-held resume, so I see no deadlock or double-resume. This fixes a lost-continuation hang when a suspended URLSession task is cancelled before attach, which is an availability improvement (T-016/T-010 adjacent). The 416/206 validation, the byte bounds, `.part` handling and the decided/setupError precedence are untouched in the visible hunks. Weight integrity (A-004, T-012, T-027) depends on the caller's manifest hash verification, which is not weakened by this diff. The other changes are docs and a changelog (model-registry.md, test.md, changelog.d), which make no new security claims and keep the caveat that component tests do not qualify live downloads or serving. The new test file uses a reserved `.invalid` host, never resumes a network task, uses UUID temp directories cleaned in close(), and has no secrets or trust-boundary interaction. No change touches TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011 or TB-012 or the T-041 cache posture. Remaining unverified contracts, outside the supplied evidence: ModelDownloader.streamDownload/downloadFile (attach called exactly once, CancellationError propagation without retry, writer-lease unwinding) and whether a resumed `.part` file is re-verified against the manifest hash before use. Neither is changed in the supplied diff, so I record them as coverage limits, not regressions. The replayed integration source is incomplete (12 units omitted), which is another reason no stronger conclusion is drawn.
